test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 17 May, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper allows 20 percent discount on the marked price of an article and he suffers a loss of 12 percent. If the article is sold at marked price, then what will be the profit percentage?
solution:
Given

Discount = 20%

Loss = 12%

Selling Price = Marked price

Formula used

Selling price = (100 - D%)/100 × M.P

where M.P = Marked price and D = discount

Calculation

Let the Cost price be 100.

S.P = (100 - 12) over100x 100 = 88.

S.P = 88.

M.P = 88 × 100/(100 - 20)

M.P = 8800/80

M.P = 110

Since the article is sold at marked price.

Profit = 110 - 100

Profit = 10

Profit% = 10/100 × 100

**Profit = 10%**

**∴ Profit percent is 10%.**

M.P = 100 × 22/25 × 5/4

⇒ 110

Since the article is sold at the marked price.

Profit% = 10/100 × 100

⇒ 10%

∴ Profit percent is 10%.
